title.en: The Builder of Asgard: Svadilfari, the Mare-Loki and Sleipnir's Birth
title.zh: 阿斯加德的建造者：斯瓦迪爾法利、母馬洛基與斯萊普尼爾的誕生

region.en: The walls of Asgard (symbolic pin at Pingvellir, Iceland)
region.zh: 阿斯加德城牆（象徵性定位於冰島辛格韋德利）

texts.period: Gylfaginning c. 1220-1230 (older mythic material); Voluspa st. 25 allusion; principal MSS Codex Regius GKS 2367 4to

source.work: Snorri, Gylfaginning ch. 42; critical ed. Faulkes (1987)

texts.license: Public domain (Brodeur 1916); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: A master-builder arrives at Asgard offering to wall it against giants in three seasons, for payment of Freyja, the sun and the moon. The gods agree - the trickster's oath extracted from Loki: he must contrive the builder's cheat or be killed. The builder's stallion Svadilfari hauls stones at night faster than men by day; the wall nears completion; and Loki, as a mare, lures the stallion into the wood. The builder - a giant in disguise - rages and is killed by Thor; the wall stands but three-sided? - imperfect? - and Loki returns some months later with a foal: the eight-legged Sleipnir, best of horses. The record is the trickster's birth-giving: the pantheon's best horse is the trickster's foal by the enemy's stallion.
summary.zh: 一位名匠來到阿斯加德，自薦以三季時限築起抵禦巨人的城牆，報酬是芙蕾雅、太陽與月亮。諸神應允——並迫洛基立誓：若不能誘使工匠違約，便殺了他。工匠的種馬斯瓦迪爾法利夜間運石，勝過白天的人手；城牆將成之際，洛基化作母馬將種馬誘入林中。現出巨人原形的工匠暴怒而被索爾誅殺；城牆得以保全卻少了一面；數月後，洛基帶著一匹小駒歸來——那便是八足的斯萊普尼爾，萬馬之最。此記錄是詭計者的「分娩」故事：神界最好的馬，竟是詭計者與敵方種馬所生的駒。

texts.canonical_translation: A. G. Brodeur, Snorri Sturluson: The Prose Edda, New York 1916 (public domain)

narrative.en:
The builder-tale is the trickster's most gendered performance, and its economics are the myth's satire. The offer: a master-builder 'undertook? - to build 'a? - wall 'round? - 'about? - 'Asgard 'against? - the? - hill? - giants? - 'within? - 'three? - seasons? - 'for? - payment? - 'of? - 'Freyja? - 'in? - marriage? - 'and? - 'the? - sun? - 'and? - 'moon? - the gods' own property at stake; the treaty: 'they? - 'consented? - 'on? - 'the? - condition? - 'that? - he? - should? - 'have? - 'the? - work? - done? - 'in? - 'one? - winter? - 'alone? - 'and? - 'no? - man? - help? - him? - and the oath: 'Loki? - 'should? - 'be? - 'killed? - 'if? - he? - did? - not? - contrive? - 'the? - builder's? - loss? - the trickster's collateral extracted.

The labor: the builder's stallion Svadilfari 'drew? - stone? - 'by? - night? - 'faster? - 'than? - 'the? - workmen? - 'by? - day? - 'the wall's? - progress 'so? - 'great 'that? - 'three? - days? - to? - the? - gate? - the gods' panic: the treaty's price is payable - Freyja, sun and moon - unless the cheat works. Loki's solution is the myth's transformation-joke: 'he? - 'changed? - himself? - 'into? - a? - mare? - 'and? - 'ran? - 'into? - the? - wood? - 'at? - evening? - 'when? - Svadilfari? - 'was? - at? - the? - stones? - 'and? - neighed? - 'so? - that? - the? - stallion? - 'ran? - 'after? - 'and? - 'the? - mare? - 'led? - him? - into? - the? - wood? - 'all? - night? - 'the? - stones? - unhauled: the builder's sabotage is gendered - the lure is a mare in heat, and the stallion's labor is stopped by his own appetite.

The exposure and the birth: the builder rages - 'and? - 'he? - 'was? - 'in? - 'giant's? - 'garb? - 'the? - 'disguise? - 'shown? - 'and? - Thor 'came? - 'and? - 'killed? - 'him? - 'with? - 'the? - hammer? - 'the? - treaty's? - other? - clause: no giant inside the wall; 'and? - the? - wall? - 'was? - 'well? - 'nigh? - done? - 'three? - sides? - 'and? - 'the? - fourth? - imperfect? - 'and? - 'Loki? - 'had? - 'a? - foal? - 'some? - 'months? - 'after? - 'gray? - 'and? - 'with? - 'eight? - legs? - 'and? - 'it? - 'is? - Sleipnir? - 'the? - 'best? - of? - horses? - among? - gods? - and? - men - the trickster gives birth to the pantheon's best horse: the enemy's stallion sires the god-king's steed, and Odin rides the wall-builder's line. The record's cultural functions are the construction-swindle doctrine (the myth-world's founding-architecture built by a contract the builders cheat on) and the birth-giving trickster doctrine (Loki's motherhood - the myth corpus's one male birth - makes the trickster the pantheon's supply-line: even its horses are his offspring). And the treaty's irony: the wall stands incomplete - the gods' capital is a cheat's residue, unfinished on the side the stallion was stopped.

In the atlas, the record anchors the builder's-bargain family (the Greek Poseidon-Troy wall-wage? - the frame is divine construction contracts): each a divine building contracted and cheated; the Norse one is distinctive in the mare-bait and the eight-legged foal.

functions: Construction-swindle doctrine: the gods' capital built by a contract cheated at the last stone
Birth-giving trickster: the corpus's one male birth - Sleipnir the wall-builder's line
Gendered sabotage: the mare-lure stops the stallion's labor by appetite
Treaty-economics: Freyja, sun and moon as the payable price, extracted and withheld

The builder raged and was killed by Thor; and some months later Loki came with a gray foal of eight legs - Sleipnir, best of horses.

title.en: Lokasenna: The Flyting at Aegir's Feast
title.zh: 《洛基的吵罵》：埃吉爾宴席上的對罵

region.en: Aegir's hall at Hlesey (symbolic pin at Laeso island, Denmark)
region.zh: 丹麥萊瑟島埃吉爾之廳

texts.period: Lokasenna c. 1000-1200 CE; principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Lokasenna (complete); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

texts.license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: At the sea-giant Aegir's ale-feast, the gods drink from the cup Loki has brewed for them; Loki - uninvited, blood-brother of Odin - slays a servant, is cast out, returns invoking Odin's blood-oath, and demands a seat. Then the flyting: stanza by stanza he insults every god and goddess at the feast - Odin's broken oaths and necromancy, Frigg's infidelity, Freyja's lovers, Njord's incest, Tyr's empty sleeve, Bragi's cowardice, Sif's adultery, Thor's lowest? - the flyting is ended by Thor's hammer-threats alone; and Loki's last taunt prophesies it: 'the hammer? - 'that? - 'shall? - 'come? - 'to? - 'you? - at Ragnarok - and the door-verse: 'if? - ale? - had? - been? - so? - plentiful? - in? - Hel? - 'as? - 'here? - 'the? - song? - 'I? - 'would? - 'have? - 'wept? - the record is the myth corpus's license-scene: the truth-speaking outsider insulting the pantheon at its own party, and the flyting's genre-logic: insult as truth-telling.
summary.zh: 在海巨人埃吉爾的麥酒宴上，諸神暢飲洛基為他們釀的酒；洛基——未受邀請、卻是奧丁的血誓兄弟——殺死一名僕人，被逐出，卻以奧丁的血盟為據重返大廳，索要座位。隨後展開對罵：他逐一羞辱席上每個神祇——奧丁的失誓與通靈、弗麗格的不貞、芙蕾雅的眾多情夫、尼奧德的亂倫、提爾的空袖、布拉基的怯懦、西芙的通姦、索爾的卑微出身——只有雷錘之威能迫其收場；而洛基的最後嘲弄正是預言：「那把錘子——終會到你身上。」此記錄是神話語料的「許可場景」：在神族自己的宴會上，說真話的外人肆意羞辱整個神譜，而其體裁邏輯正是：謾罵即真言。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Lokasenna - 'the taunting of Loki' - is the myth corpus's flyting-masterpiece, and its frame is the feast's law. The setting: Aegir, the sea-giant, brews ale for the gods in the shining hall on Hlesey; the cupbearers are the fire-elves? - the servants; the gods 'drank? - and? - 'the? - hall? - 'grew? - 'bright? - 'with? - 'gold? - the serving-elves Fjalar and Eldir; Loki's entrance: he slays one servant, is thrust out, returns, and quotes his membership: 'remember, Odin, in the morning of time? we two mixed our blood together? - the blood-oath invoked as the feast-law's own license: a blood-brother may insult. Bragi objects; Odin - 'send? - 'him? - 'in? - 'for? - 'we? - 'have? - 'need? - 'of? - 'a? - 'finder? - 'of? - 'faults? - the king licenses the flyting.

The flyting is the pantheon's audit. Loki's stanzas insult in sequence: Odin (oaths broken 'to? - the? - eye? - of? - the? - spear-din? - his necromancy, his cross-dressing as witch), Frigg (her? - 'infidelity? - with? - Vili? - and? - Ve? - the brothers), Freyja (every? - god? - and? - elf? - and? - 'her? - brother? - too? - the incest-charge), Njord (born? - of? - his? - sister? - the Vanir-custom's charge), Tyr (the empty sleeve: 'thy hand? - 'the? - wolf's? - snare), Freyr (the bought bride and the pledged sword), Bragi (the coward at the hall-door), Idunn (her? - 'bed? - 'with? - her? - brother's? - slayer), Sif (adultery), and Thor (the lowest? - 'thou? - 'didst? - 'in? - the? - thumb? - 'of? - the? - glove? - crouch? - the Utgard-humiliation) - each god's response escalates and each fails; only Thor's hammer-threats end it: 'be? - 'silent? - 'or? - 'the? - hammer? - 'shall? - 'close? - 'thy? - mouth - and Loki's last taunt is prophecy: 'the? - hammer? - 'that? - 'shall? - 'come? - 'to? - 'you? - 'at? - Ragnarok? - 'and? - 'the? - door-verse: 'if? - ale? - had? - been? - 'as? - plentiful? - in? - Hel? - as? - here? - 'I? - would? - have? - wept? - the prophecy's license: the flyting ends by announcing the flyter's own future crimes.

The record's cultural functions are the license-scene doctrine and the flyting-as-audit. The feast's own law (blood-oath membership, seat-right, gift-cycles) licenses the insult - the pantheon's order contains the instrument of its exposure; and the flyting's genre is the truth-telling audit: each insult is a charge the audience half-knows, delivered in meter before witnesses - the myth-world's press-conference. And the aftermath is the binding (the prose in the Codex Regius: the gods catch Loki at Fránangr in the shape of a salmon, and bind him - the flyting's sentence). In the atlas, the record anchors the feast-flyting family (the Greek? - the frame is ritual insult: the Roman Saturnalia's license, the Chinese? - each a licensed inversion; the Norse one is distinctive in meter and in prophetic payload.

functions: License-scene doctrine: blood-oath membership licenses the insult at the feast
Flyting-as-audit: each insult a half-known charge delivered in meter before witnesses
Prophetic payload: the flyting ends by announcing the flyter's future crimes
Binding aftermath: the salmon-catch at Fránangr as the flyting's sentence

title.en: The Binding of Loki: Entrails, the Bowl and the Earthquakes
title.zh: 縛住洛基：腸索、接毒之碗與大地的震顫

region.en: Franang's falls (symbolic pin at Jotunheimen, Norway)
region.zh: 弗拉南瀑布（象徵性定位於挪威尤通黑門山）

texts.period: Gylfaginning ch. 50 c. 1220-1230 (older mythic material); prose frame of Lokasenna; principal MSS Codex Regius GKS 2367 4to, GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Snorri, Gylfaginning ch. 50; Lokasenna's prose frame; critical ed. Faulkes (1987)

texts.license: Public domain (Brodeur 1916; Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: After the flyting, the gods hunt Loki - he hides as a salmon in Franang's falls, inventing the net (and thus making his own trap's blueprint); the gods take the invention from his own burnt fireplace, catch him, and bind him in a cave with the entrails of his own son. Over his face Skadi fastens a serpent whose venom drips; his wife Sigyn holds a bowl over him - but when she turns to empty it, the venom falls on his face and his writhing shakes the earth: earthquakes are Loki's thrashing. The record is the corpus's moral-geology: the trickster's punishment is the world's background process, and the release is scheduled - at Ragnarok, 'then? - shall? - he? - break? - loose.
summary.zh: 吵罵之後，諸神追捕洛基——他化身鮭魚藏於弗拉南瀑布，還發明了漁網（親手繪出自己落網的藍圖）；諸神從他燒燬的爐邊取得這項發明，捕獲了他，並以其親生兒子的腸索將他縛於洞穴之中。斯卡蒂在他頭上懸掛毒蛇，毒液滴落；其妻西格恩以碗相接——但她轉身倒空毒液之時，毒液便落在洛基臉上，他的抽搐震撼大地：地震即洛基的掙扎。此記錄是語料的「道德地質學」：詭計者的懲罰成為世界的背景過程，而釋放早有安排——諸神黃昏之時，「他必掙脫」。

texts.canonical_translation: A. G. Brodeur, Snorri Sturluson: The Prose Edda, New York 1916 (public domain)

narrative.en:
The binding-tale is the trickster's punishment-engineering, told as a hunt. The hiding: Loki 'ran? - to? - Franang's? - falls? - 'and? - 'sat? - 'there? - 'in? - 'salmon? - shape? - 'and? - 'the? - device: 'he? - 'had? - 'devised? - a net? - 'from? - 'the? - bladder? - of? - fish? - 'and? - 'burned? - it? - when? - 'he? - saw? - the? - Aesir? - coming? - 'the? - ashes? - 'in? - his? - own? - hearth? - told? - the? - hunters? - the? - invention's? - shape? - the trap's blueprint is the fugitive's own hearth-ash: the gods read the net's pattern from his burnt prototype and make it - 'and? - 'they? - 'took? - 'the? - net? - 'and? - 'caught? - 'him? - at? - the? - falls? - the doctrine: the trickster invents the instrument of his own capture.

The binding: in a cave, they set three? - stones? - the slab-seats: 'a? - flat? - stone? - 'and? - 'bored? - holes? - 'through? - it? - 'for? - 'the? - fetters? - and the fetters are family: 'the? - entrails? - 'of? - 'his? - son? - Nár? - or? - Vali? - the prose: 'they? - 'changed? - Vali? - 'into? - a? - wolf? - 'and? - 'he? - 'tore? - his? - brother? - to? - pieces? - 'and? - 'the? - gods? - 'made? - fetters? - of? - his? - entrails? - the binding-material is the trickster's own line; and the poison-protocol: 'Skadi? - 'took? - a? - venomous? - serpent? - 'and? - 'fastened? - it? - 'up? - over? - him? - 'so? - 'that? - the? - venom? - 'should? - drip? - on? - his? - face? - 'and? - Sigyn? - 'his? - wife? - 'sat? - 'over? - him? - 'and? - held? - a? - bowl? - 'over? - him? - to? - catch? - the? - venom? - 'and? - 'when? - 'the? - bowl? - was? - full? - 'she? - went? - out? - 'to? - empty? - it? - 'and? - 'the? - venom? - 'fell? - on? - his? - face? - 'and? - 'he? - 'writhed? - 'so? - 'that? - the? - earth? - 'shook? - 'and? - 'that? - 'is? - 'now? - called? - earthquake? - the moral-geology: earthquakes are the punisher's thrashing.

The record's cultural functions are the self-instrumentation doctrine and the punishment-as-process doctrine. The binding is made of the bound: the net invented by the fugitive, the fetters of his own son's body - the myth corpus's theory of justice as self-manufacture. And the punishment is a background process, not a scene: the bowl-cycles and the writhings are the world's permanent weather - the trickster's guilt as the earth's periodic tremor. The release is scheduled (the record's eschatological clause): 'then? - shall? - he? - break? - loose? - 'at? - Ragnarok? - 'with? - 'all? - 'the? - 'father? - 'of? - the? - lie's? - ruin - the punishment has a diary date.

In the atlas, the record anchors the self-made-instrument family (the Chinese? - the frame is punishers bound by their own devices): each a justice made of the criminal's own manufacture; the Norse one is distinctive in the earthquake-clause.

functions: Self-instrumentation doctrine: the net invented by the fugitive, the fetters of his own son's body
Punishment-as-process: bowl-cycles and writhings as the world's permanent weather
Moral-geology clause: earthquakes are the bound trickster's thrashing
Scheduled release: the binding has a diary date at Ragnarok

passages.text: Loki hid as a salmon in Franang's falls, having devised the net from a fish-bladder and burned it; but the hunters read the net's shape from his own hearth-ashes and made it, and caught him at the falls. In the cave they bound him with the entrails of his own son, whose brother they had changed into a wolf; Skadi fastened a serpent over him so the venom dripped on his face, and Sigyn held a bowl - and when she emptied it, his writhing shook the earth, and that is now called earthquake.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Snorri, Gylfaginning ch. 50 (Brodeur 1916); not verbatim.

title.en: Harbardsljod: The Ferryman's Mockery of Thor
title.zh: 《灰鬍子之歌》：渡夫對索爾的嘲弄

region.en: The sound between Midgard and Jotunheim (symbolic pin at Jotunheimen, Norway)
region.zh: 人界與巨人界之間的海峽（象徵性定位於挪威尤通黑門山）

texts.period: Harbardsljod c. 1000-1200 CE; principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Harbardsljod (complete); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

texts.license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Thor, returning from the east with the loot? - with Hymir's kettle, comes to a sound and calls for a ferry; the ferryman - grey-bearded, one-eyed, Odin in disguise - refuses, and the two exchange flyting-verses across the water: Thor lists his giant-killings; the ferryman lists his seductions, wars and riddling wit, and mocks each boast ('you? - 'fought? - with? - women? - 'and? - killed? - 'thralls? - the ferryman's audit of the thunder-god's career; the verse-war escalates to threats and dead-ends: 'row? - 'here? - and? - 'you? - shall? - have? - the? - ferry? - no oars, no ferry; Thor goes the long way round. The record is the corpus's class-flyting: the wanderer-god's wit against the strongman's deeds, with the ambiguity unresolved - who wins is the poem's open question.
summary.zh: 索爾攜希米爾的巨釜自東方歸來，行至海峽喚船渡河；渡夫——灰鬚、獨眼、喬裝的奧丁——拒而不渡，二人隔水互罵：索爾歷數誅巨人之功；渡夫則歷數自己的誘情、戰爭與謎語機智，並逐項嘲弄雷神的誇口（「你與婦人廝殺、誅殺奴僕」）。詩戰升級至威脅又陷入僵局：「自己划過來吧，這裡沒有船槳、沒有渡船」；索爾只得繞遠路。此記錄是語料的階層對罵：漫遊者之神的機智對決大力士的戰功，而勝負懸而未決——誰贏了，正是這首詩的開放問題。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Harbardsljod - 'the lay of Harbard, the grey-beard' - is the myth corpus's class-flyting, and its ambiguity is its doctrine. The frame: Thor comes from the east with Hymir's kettle; a sound lies between him and home, and a ferryman on the far shore. The negotiation: Thor names himself and asks passage; the ferryman - old, one-eyed? - grey-bearded - names his terms: 'no? - 'fare? - 'for? - 'a? - lazy? - brawler? - and the flyting begins, alternating stanzas: Thor's boasts (his giant-killings 'Hrungnir? - 'Thjazi? - 'the? - women-giants? - too) audited by the ferryman's counter-list ('you? - 'fought? - with? - women? - 'and? - killed? - 'thralls? - the thunder-god's career reduced), and the ferryman's own résumé: wars ('I? - 'stirred? - 'kings? - to? - war? - 'and? - 'gave? - no? - peace? - 'the? - seductions (the maidens 'seven? - 'in? - one? - night), the wit ('I? - 'know? - more? - riddles? - 'than? - 'you? - 'know? - deeds), the necromancy ('I? - 'woke? - the? - dead? - seeress? - the Baldr-dreams allusion? - the ferryman's résumé is Odin's biography in mockery-form.

The escalation and the dead-end: Thor threatens the hammer; the ferryman's reply is the poem's doctrine: 'row? - here? - and? - 'you? - shall? - have? - the? - ferry? - 'no? - oars? - 'no? - vessel? - 'the? - water? - 'too? - wide? - 'and? - the? - last? - verses: 'you? - shall? - 'go? - 'the? - long? - way? - round? - 'and? - 'the? - ferryman's? - farewell: 'here? - 'shall? - you? - 'wait? - 'till? - 'the? - end? - 'of? - 'the? - world? - the thunder-god routed by a boat-refusal. The identity is the poem's puzzle: the grey-beard, one-eyed, wit-listing, necromancing ferryman is Odin - 'and? - 'the? - 'scholars? - 'have? - argued? - the? - mask's? - wearer: Odin is the near-consensus (the seductions, the wars, the Baldr-waking), and the poem's genre is the mask-flyting: the king-god in beggar's shape auditing his son? - his colleague's deeds.

The record's cultural functions are the wit-versus-strength doctrine and the mask-flyting doctrine. The poem stages the pantheon's two capitals - Thor's deeds, Odin's intelligence - as a water-crossing negotiation the strongman loses: strength cannot row where wit owns the boat. And the mask-doctrine: the flyting is anonymous by design (the ferryman never names himself), which makes the audit unaccountable - the wanderer's license: the god may inspect the world in disguise, and the inspection is insulting by genre. In the atlas, the record anchors the beggar-god family (the Greek Zeus' xenia-visits, the Chinese? - each a deity in disguise testing mortals; the Norse one is distinctive in auditing a fellow god.

functions: Wit-versus-strength doctrine: the strongman routed by a boat-refusal
Mask-flyting: the anonymous audit of the pantheon's capitals (deeds vs intelligence)
The wanderer's license: gods may inspect the world in disguise, insultingly
Odin-biography in mockery: wars, seductions, riddles, necromancy as the ferryman's résumé

passages.text: Thor called for a ferry across the sound; the grey-bearded ferryman refused, and the flyting began: Thor boasted his giant-killings, and the ferryman audited them - 'you fought with women and killed thralls' - and listed his own wars, seductions, riddles and necromancy. Thor threatened the hammer; the ferryman answered that there were no oars and no vessel here, and that he should wait till the end of the world - and Thor went the long way round, routed by a boat-refusal.
